speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with blisters on your forearm and ulcers on mucosal surfaces. To narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any fever or fatigue?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS) is unlikely given the age and specific mucosal involvement; Herpes Zoster is possible but less likely to cause widespread blistering without dermatomal restriction. The combination of recent captopril initiation, mucosal ulceration, and skin blisters strongly suggests a drug-induced reaction, likely Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Liver Function Tests. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the forearm blisters and oral/mucosal lesions.
